QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_12

question.text: Penalty on seller for delivery default in non-agricultural commodity futures is:

explanation.text: The Logic: For non-agri commodities, seller delivery default attracts 3% of the Settlement Price plus a replacement cost. Replacement cost is the excess of the higher of the last spot prices on the commodity pay-out date and the following day over the Settlement Price, only when that higher spot price is above the Settlement Price. The Trap: The non-agri replacement cost reference is the higher last spot price across the pay-out date and the next day, not the multi-day "three highest of five succeeding days" average used for agri commodities. The direction of the difference also matters — replacement cost only kicks in when the spot reference is above, not below, the Settlement Price. Note: Apportionment of the 3% slab follows the regulator's structure: a share to the SGF, a small portion to the clearing corporation, and the balance plus replacement cost to the non-defaulting buyer.
